# Naming analyzer: better variable, function and class names

Curated by Skill Harbor — @softaworks's naming-analyzer skill: a naming-convention expert for your agent. It analyzes existing names (variables, constants, functions, methods, classes, interfaces, types, files, directories, database tables and columns, API endpoints), identifies issues (unclear or vague names, misleading names that don't match behavior, obscuring abbreviations, inconsistent conventions, too-short/too-long names, Hungarian notation misuse, single-letter variables outside loops), checks conventions per language (JS/TS camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, Python snake_case, Java camelCase, Go PascalCase-exported with all-caps acronyms like HTTPServer), and provides suggestions with reasoning. It ships a full naming-analysis report format (summary counts, critical/major/minor issues with file:line, current vs suggestion vs reason, convention violations), naming patterns to follow, DO/DON'T best practices, a boolean/function/class/constant decision tree, and offers to create a refactoring script to apply the changes. Honest caveats: pure advisory guidance — it suggests names, it doesn't run the refactors itself (the refactoring script is offered, not automatic); examples skew JavaScript but the convention tables cover Python, Java and Go too. MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
